cases.candidate_script:
set -u
H=/opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/dnssec-anchor-bridge-peer.py
/usr/bin/python3 "$H" prep || exit 98
/usr/bin/python3 "$H" serve 127.0.0.2 5340 ready 2> "$HOME/anchor-peer.err" & peer=$!
trap 'kill "$peer" 2>/dev/null; wait "$peer" 2>/dev/null' EXIT
/usr/bin/python3 "$H" waitudp 127.0.0.2 5340 || exit 98
control=$(/usr/bin/python3 "$H" control 127.0.0.2 5340 anchor-bridge) || exit 98
[[ $control == control-ok ]] || { printf '%s\n' "$control"; exit 98; }
echo control-ok
export PATH="$HOME/pbin" BASHDNS_SERVER_PORT=5340 BASHDNS_TRUST_ANCHOR="$PWD/anchor.ds" BASHDNS_0X20=0
if dns query roguekey.test A -s 127.0.0.2 -t 3000 --validate > "$HOME/rogue.out" 2> "$HOME/rogue.err"; then echo rogue=accepted; exit 1; else echo rogue=rejected; fi
if dns query multisig.test A -s 127.0.0.2 -t 3000 --validate > "$HOME/multi.out" 2> "$HOME/multi.err"; then echo multi=accepted; else echo multi=rejected; exit 1; fi
cases.purpose: Only a DS-anchored DNSKEY may authenticate a candidate DNSKEY RRset; an additional untrusted signature before a valid one must not cause rejection.
cases.oracle: Independent BIND delv validates/rejects a deterministic ECDSA fixture before the candidate is queried.
cases.comparison: Reject the DNSKEY RRset signed solely by a non-anchored key, accept the set with a second anchored signature, and preserve raw peer and candidate diagnostics.
